title: No aggregate cap on per-client buffer percentages allows total set-aside to reach 100% of underlyingReceived, reducing recipient take to zero with no revert
story: story-042 — per-client setAsideBuffer added to skimSurplus
description: setSetAsideBuffer enforces bufferPercent <= 100 per client (AYieldStrategy.sol#L255). The sum of setAsideBufferSize[client] across the authorized-client set is not capped. With multiple clients at high buffer percentages, totalBufferShares can approach totalShares, in which case toRecipient (ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy.sol#L518-L520) collapses to zero and the entire swap output is redirected to clients[]. The skim completes successfully with no revert, but the withdrawer's recipient parameter is effectively a no-op.
impact: No direct loss — all funds remain protocol-owned (buffered slices go to authorized clients). Recipient and any downstream integrator pricing in expected yield from skimSurplus sees zero proceeds despite the swap consuming all surplus value and incurring slippage. Companion enabler for M-04's worst-case parametric leak (f → 1).
parametricBound: toRecipient ≈ underlyingReceived * (1 - sum(principal[i] * setAsideBufferSize[i]) / (totalDeposited * 100)). At sum-weighted buffer == 100%, toRecipient == 0.
attackPath: 1. Owner configures multiple authorized clients with high setAsideBufferSize values whose sum-weighted product reaches or exceeds 100% of underlyingReceived.
2. setSetAsideBuffer accepts each call (only per-client <=100% check) — no aggregate cap revert.
3. On the next skimSurplus, _distributeBuffer transfers totalSetAside == underlyingReceived to clients; toRecipient collapses to 0.
4. The skim completes without revert; SurplusSkimmed event fires with the recipient parameter that now received nothing.
assumptions: Owner is benign but may misconfigure (operator/keeper-driven setter calls are a realistic source of malformed input).
externalRequirements: Owner exercises setSetAsideBuffer across enough clients to push the sum-weighted buffer to or near 100%.
recommendation: Track an aggregate buffer-weight metric on setSetAsideBuffer calls and enforce a configurable ceiling (e.g. aggregateBufferCapBps), OR add a require in _distributeBuffer that toRecipient > 0 (or >= someMin) when totalBufferShares > 0 so an all-clients-at-100 misconfiguration reverts loudly. Per memory feedback_revert_over_silent_clamp.md, prefer revert-on-malformed-config over silent clamp.

ledgerLink.kind: operator footgun within centralization envelope; companion to M-04
ledgerLink.note: C-01 still covers the owner-trust framing, but this is a setter-design gap orthogonal to centralization risk: even a benevolent owner has no defense against a fat-finger across clients. Together M-04 + L-03 describe the slippage-bound failure mode under buffer mis-sizing.

poc.note: Low severity; PoC not required for QA bundle. Demonstrable via unit test if author wants concrete proof.
